title: TEAM7 · Courtside IQ architecture
subtitle: User workflows, code evidence and operating limits · static offline explorer

nodes.title: Host workspace
nodes.responsibility: The browser maps video time to the available evidence. The host reviews identities, annotations, narration and public actions.
nodes.limits: Private suggestions are not authoritative events. Unknown identities must remain unknown.

nodes.title: Amazon CloudFront
nodes.responsibility: CloudFront routes the web application, media and uncached API paths to their configured origins.
nodes.limits: CloudFront is global. This logical group is not a VPC or availability-zone diagram.

nodes.title: API Gateway → Lambda
nodes.responsibility: HTTP routes validate access and dispatch upload, evidence, production and broadcast operations to Python handlers.
nodes.limits: A session ID is not an owner credential. Public read and owner write have different access rules.

nodes.title: Amazon S3
nodes.responsibility: Uploads, extracted frames, evidence artifacts and shared productions are stored under separate object keys.
nodes.limits: An object key is not public authorization. Large original files still incur storage and transfer costs.

nodes.title: AWS Step Functions
nodes.responsibility: The state machine coordinates media preparation, evidence joining and batched vision indexing, with explicit failure recording.
nodes.limits: Retries do not guarantee automatic correction of bad identities, game matching or model claims.

nodes.title: AWS Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.responsibility: MediaConvert produces a source-resolution MP4 and JPEG samples for analysis. A separate render branch transcodes an already-composited WebM.
nodes.limits: It does not interpret the custom editing JSON. Analysis currently samples 4 fps over at most the first ten minutes.

evidence.claim: Source processing and alternate render branch.

nodes.title: Amazon Rekognition
nodes.responsibility: The pipeline reads visible scoreboard text to estimate period and game-clock alignment.
nodes.limits: OCR is fallible. A timestamp match is not a verified ball-release frame.

evidence.claim: Scoreboard region and sampled OCR calls.

nodes.title: Official NBA evidence join
nodes.responsibility: Python joins the inferred game clock, roster and hints to the NBA snapshots actually available to the application.
nodes.limits: Coverage is bounded by ingested snapshots. Filenames are hints, not proof; an unfamiliar clip may remain unmatched.

nodes.title: Amazon SageMaker AI
nodes.responsibility: A custom inference server provides detection, segmentation and pose outputs used by the vision index and selected-player presentation.
nodes.limits: Outputs depend on enabled endpoints and loaded models. Tracks do not guarantee identity or cross-shot re-identification.

nodes.title: Amazon Bedrock · Qwen3-VL
nodes.responsibility: The Bedrock Converse call receives selected JPEG frames and structured evidence; normalization checks references before use.
nodes.limits: Visual interpretations are estimates. It must not invent official statistics or confirmed identities.

evidence.claim: Converse image input and output normalization.
The asynchronous scene job calls the image model.

nodes.title: AgentCore + Strands
nodes.responsibility: AgentCore hosts the Python agent application. Strands GraphBuilder orchestrates evidence_planner, tactical_analyst and evidence_editor for possession preparation.
nodes.limits: The live tool-using agent and preparation graph are distinct paths. AgentCore uses PUBLIC networking here.

evidence.claim: Actual Strands GraphBuilder nodes and invocation.
PUBLIC network configuration; no private VPC claim.

nodes.title: Validation + Bedrock Guardrails
nodes.responsibility: Preparation checks evidence references, allows one editor repair, then applies the configured guardrail before persisting a report.
nodes.limits: Safety filtering does not certify basketball facts or calibrated probabilities. Independent accuracy evaluation is still missing.

evidence.claim: Program validation, one repair and guardrail application.

nodes.title: DynamoDB + S3 evidence
nodes.responsibility: Application records retain analysis state and annotations; S3 artifacts keep source-linked evidence and reports.
nodes.limits: Persisted model output is still a draft until reviewed. Source linkage is not an independent accuracy test.

nodes.title: Host review & public approval
nodes.responsibility: The host can correct identities, edit narration and approve an overlay. Private agent suggestions cannot directly invoke a public publish tool.
nodes.limits: Human approval reduces accidental publishing; it does not replace evidence checking.

nodes.title: Editable narration cache
nodes.responsibility: Reviewed text survives a model rerun. Annotation revisions invalidate stale analysis, and Polly audio is keyed by the final text and voice.
nodes.limits: Different annotations and edited scripts must not reuse stale audio. Signed delivery URLs need renewal.

evidence.claim: Reviewed text preservation and narration caching.

nodes.title: Amazon Polly
nodes.responsibility: The application synthesizes approved text with configured Polly voices and serves cached audio to the host.
nodes.limits: Voice cloning and a custom voice model are not delivered by this path. Browser audio may need a user gesture.

nodes.title: WebSocket API + Lambda
nodes.responsibility: The real-time control path delivers asynchronous agent work results and approved session events.
nodes.limits: Session-specific notifications are not the shared public program clock. Delivery requires correct session routing.

nodes.title: Cognito → Transcribe
nodes.responsibility: A narrowly scoped Cognito Identity Pool role allows the browser to stream microphone audio to Amazon Transcribe when the host enables it.
nodes.limits: Needs browser permission, valid temporary credentials and service access. A wake-word label alone does not prove reliable wake detection.

nodes.title: Original media + JSON timeline
nodes.responsibility: The browser records playback, holds, rate changes, approved visuals and mixed program audio into courtside-project/v1.
nodes.limits: This is a custom replay format, not a standard editing interchange. Flattened video export re-encodes.

nodes.title: Shared production library
nodes.responsibility: The owner uploads assets and a manifest. Server validation checks objects before marking a production ready for shared read.
nodes.limits: A local-only draft is not visible on another browser. Owner writes remain authenticated.

nodes.title: DynamoDB · program clock
nodes.responsibility: The public broadcast stores the selected production and uses a server start time with elapsed modulo duration for loop position.
nodes.limits: This is recorded-program synchronization, not frame-accurate live streaming. No IVS or MediaLive pipeline is claimed.

evidence.claim: Durable broadcast selection and modulo clock.

nodes.title: Public /broadcast viewer
nodes.summary: No host session in the URL
nodes.responsibility: Viewers join the same selected production. The player refreshes expiring asset URLs and reconstructs the timeline or plays a rendered asset.
nodes.limits: Autoplay starts muted where required; a viewer click enables sound. Network buffering still affects synchronization.

evidence.claim: Public player asset renewal and playback.

nodes.title: Roboflow · optional detection
nodes.responsibility: The analysis pipeline can send up to eight selected frames to an external Roboflow inference API when explicitly enabled.
nodes.limits: External data transfer and usage-based charges apply. This is not a mandatory analysis dependency.

nodes.title: Tripo · asset authoring
nodes.responsibility: Tripo was used separately to author mascot assets. The application loads resulting GLB assets or lets users import a model.
nodes.limits: This is an authoring-time tool, not an automatically called per-frame runtime service.

evidence.claim: Team mascot asset provenance and integration.

nodes.title: IAM · Secrets · CloudWatch
nodes.responsibility: CDK declares permissions, secret access, logs and a pipeline failure alarm. These are independent operational controls.
nodes.limits: A declared alarm without an action is not verified paging. No measured cost or full least-privilege audit is claimed.

evidence.claim: Agent permissions and secret access declarations.

nodes.title: Amazon SQS · failure records
nodes.responsibility: AgentWorker uses an SQS failure destination to retain unhandled asynchronous Lambda invocation failures.
nodes.limits: It is not the normal request queue. No automatic replay consumer is established by this wiring.

folders.title: 1. Upload & analyze
folders.description: Turn uploaded footage into reviewable evidence.

steps.note: The host opens an uploaded clip; access is checked.
Media is stored before the analysis job starts.
The control plane requests the state machine.
MediaConvert is polled; failures are recorded.
Scoreboard readings estimate game-clock alignment.
Only ingested NBA data can be matched; missing evidence remains missing.
Detection, segmentation and pose provide observations, not guaranteed identities.
Selected JPEGs and structured context can be interpreted by Qwen3-VL.
Store the matching result and retain provenance.
Tracks and masks are stored separately from official facts.

boundaries.title: AWS Cloud · logical application group (not VPC topology)

folders.title: 2. Ask, edit & approve
folders.description: A private answer becomes a reviewed broadcast cue.

steps.note: The current timestamp and evidence revision accompany the request.
The asynchronous worker returns updates via the real-time path.
The live tool agent is distinct from the preparation graph shown in node details.
The scene job worker calls Qwen3-VL; live agent tools read cached observations rather than invoking this model themselves.
The preparation graph validates references and applies its configured guardrail.
A saved report remains a draft until the host reviews it.
Reviewed text survives reruns; revised annotations invalidate stale analysis.
The human host owns the final wording and public action.
Audio uses the final text and configured voice; this is not voice cloning.
Permission and temporary credentials are required.

boundaries.title: AWS Cloud · logical application group (not VPC topology)

folders.title: 3. Record & share
folders.description: Keep editing local; share validated assets to all sessions.

steps.note: Program time includes held frames; original source pixels remain separate.
A local draft becomes shareable only after assets are uploaded.
The server checks registered assets before marking the production READY.
The default replay reconstructs the custom timeline.
Authenticated owner selection changes the shared public program.
A session-free viewer joins the loop; this is recorded playback.
CloudFront or signed object URLs deliver the registered media.
Muted autoplay may require a click to enable commentary audio.
The render branch accepts precomposited WebM, not the custom JSON itself.

boundaries.title: AWS Cloud · logical application group (not VPC topology)

folders.title: 4. Optional tools & operations
folders.description: External tools and failure paths have separate boundaries.

steps.note: Selected frames leave AWS only when the host enables this integration.
The custom SageMaker path remains separate from optional Roboflow.
Approved asset creation yields models later served as static assets.
The browser renders GLB assets; it does not call Tripo per frame.
SQS is an onFailure destination; no normal request queue or replay consumer is claimed.
This operational relationship represents a metric/alarm declaration, not verified paging.

boundaries.title: AWS Cloud · logical application group (not VPC topology)
